newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk recommends 2-rbl 96 privileged div.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk recommends 2-rbl 96 privileged div.

text.p: The board of Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group will recommend a 1996 dividend of two roubles ($0.0003 at today's rates) per privileged share, down from 1995's 438 roubles, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
Anatoly Komrakov also said the board would recommend no dividend be paid for ordinary shares for 1996 for the second year in a row. Both types of shares have a face value of 250 roubles.

Norilsk -- a top global producer of nickel, platinum, palladium, cobalt, copper and other metals -- holds its annual shareholders' meeting on Friday, at which Komrakov said the board would recommend the dividends.
Financially-troubled RAO Norilsky Nikel is struggling to enact a restructuring programme aimed at dragging the company out of crisis.

It plans to expand nickel output by 20 percent in 1997 to a huge 213,000 tonnes, which would make it the largest nickel producer in the world, but its flagship plant has been hit by cuts in natural gas supplies.

Norilsk said in May it was heading for bankruptcy after 1996 consolidated losses according to Russian accounting standards of 3.29 trillion roubles ($571 million) on the back of enormous social spending costs.
